fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: spatial cell or spot observations with expression or phenotype features plus spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify, characterize, and compare cellular niches across spatial omics samples
rows.Main Output: niche labels, niche composition summaries, neighborhood-enrichment and shape summaries
rows.Key Difference: Uses scalable niche clustering and comparison across data types rather than TCN discovery, single-cell niche graph learning, atlas-scale contrastive embeddings, or communication-prior embeddings.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Genetics method paper and the paper reports open-source CellCharter code. Layer 2 synthesis: resource and comparator labels reflect topic-level comparison, not BioHarness runtime validation.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task is broad cellular-niche discovery or cross-sample niche comparison from spatial omics maps.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard tissue-domain labels, ligand-receptor communication, ordered topology motifs, or transcriptome-to-space reconstruction.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: cell/spot niche composition and local feature neighborhoods
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Niche labels can be sensitive to feature preprocessing, cluster granularity, and sample-composition imbalance.

rows.Method Family: Covariance niche representation plus conditional variational autoencoder
rows.Main Input: spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed spatial data plus matched or relevant scRNA-seq data
rows.Main Use in This Topic: represent cellular neighborhoods through covariance structure and infer spatial context or missing expression
rows.Main Output: COVET niche representations, ENVI latent embedding, imputed expression, projected spatial context
rows.Key Difference: Centers neighborhood representation on gene-gene covariance within local niches and a joint spatial/single-cell latent model.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Biotechnology paper and the article reports ENVI/COVET Python code. Layer 2 synthesis: placement in this topic emphasizes niche representation rather than treating imputation as the primary task.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the scientific question needs covariance-defined niches and a spatial plus scRNA-seq representation for inference or imputation.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When no matched reference or query transfer objective is available, or when the primary endpoint is hard domain labels or CCC edges.
rows.Interpretation Anchor: covariance structure and inferred spatial context
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Reference mismatch and covariance choices can shape inferred niches and imputed genes.

rows.Main Input: multi-sample spatial transcriptomics count matrices with coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: extract shared gene loadings and sample-specific spatial factors across multiple sections or samples
rows.Main Output: multi-sample spatial factors and gene loadings
rows.Key Difference: Extends NSF to multiple samples without requiring spatial alignment by sharing gene loadings while allowing sample-specific spatial structure.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology paper and the paper links the mNSF package plus analysis code. Direct resource evidence notes TensorFlow/GPU design and scaling pressure; downstream selection cues are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When multiple spatial samples need shared factor interpretation without assuming reliable spatial alignment.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When millions of cells or very high-resolution maps require a first-pass scalable soft-neighborhood method.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: sample-specific spatial factors with shared gene loadings
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Classic factorization interpretability limits remain, and spatial factors may mix biological and technical variation.

rows.Main Input: spatial transcriptomics matrix with 2D or 3D coordinates, optionally across multiple samples
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify overlapping spatial neighborhoods and multicellular gene signatures at large scale
rows.Main Output: soft neighborhood signatures, hard cluster labels if postprocessed, spatially variable gene patterns
rows.Key Difference: Keeps overlapping soft gene signatures and scales to large cell counts instead of forcing hard niche borders first.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the 2026 Genome Biology paper and the paper reports an R package plus large-scale evaluations. Layer 2 synthesis: low scale sensitivity is a coarse cue and not a BioHarness performance claim.
rows.Best First Choice When: When overlapping spatial gene programs or soft multicellular neighborhoods are preferred, especially for large datasets.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the main goal is communication-pathway interpretation, ecological hotspot metrics, or scRNA-to-space reconstruction.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Soft signatures are biologically rich but may be awkward when downstream work expects mutually exclusive domains.

rows.Main Input: spatial genomics count matrix with spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: derive interpretable spatial factors from a single spatial sample or limited sample set
rows.Main Output: nonnegative spatial factors, feature loadings, optional hybrid spatial/nonspatial factor summaries
rows.Key Difference: Provides the original probabilistic nonnegative spatial factor model rather than multi-sample extension or scalable neighborhood smoothing.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods NSF paper and the article reports code plus high memory examples. Layer 2 synthesis: it is kept as the baseline spatial-factorization branch rather than a default for all neighborhood tasks.
rows.Best First Choice When: When a single-sample interpretable spatial factorization baseline is needed and resource burden is acceptable.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the dataset is atlas-scale, explicitly multi-sample, or requires cellular-niche labels rather than factors.
rows.Interpretation Anchor: gene loadings and spatial factor maps
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Factor labels are not inherently cell niches and can be hard to interpret without external biological annotation.

rows.Main Input: spatial omics observations, coordinates, and microenvironment graph features
rows.Main Use in This Topic: model microenvironments and their relationships for heterogeneity, domain, and differential microenvironment analysis
rows.Main Output: microenvironment representations, spatial domains, heterogeneity and differential microenvironment summaries
rows.Key Difference: Uses optimal-transport microenvironment modeling as a multi-task spatial omics framework rather than ecological diversity or graph-neural niche learning.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper after metadata repair. Layer 2 synthesis: SOTIP is retained in Graph / Neighborhood only for microenvironment modeling and differential microenvironment analysis; hard spatial-domain labels route to Domain / Clustering.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task centers on microenvironment graph modeling or differential microenvironment relationships rather than hard tissue-region labeling.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard tissue/domain/region labels or spatial clustering; route those tasks to Domain / Clustering.
rows.Interpretation Anchor: microenvironment composition and differential ME analysis
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: SOTIP overlaps spatial domain identification; domain-label benchmarks are task-adjacent evidence only and cannot rank Graph / Neighborhood branches globally.

rows.Main Input: spatial omics cell maps and optional single-cell multiomics integration inputs
rows.Main Use in This Topic: quantify tissue-state spatial diversity, hotspots, cold spots, and ecological neighborhood shifts
rows.Main Output: ecological diversity metrics, hotspot/coldspot maps, neighborhood and cohabitation summaries
rows.Key Difference: Frames spatial neighborhoods through ecology-inspired diversity and hotspot metrics rather than clustering alone.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Genetics paper and the article reports MESA documentation and GitHub. Layer 2 synthesis: use here is strongest for metric-based neighborhood-state analysis, not generic niche discovery.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the question asks for spatial diversity, tissue-state shifts, hotspots, cold spots, or cohabitation metrics.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the desired result is hard domain segmentation, LR/CCC inference, or explicit topology motif discovery.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: patch or kNN neighborhood ecological diversity
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Ecological analogies are useful descriptors but should not be read as mechanistic causality without perturbational support.

rows.Main Input: single- or multi-sample spatial omics graph with gene expression and optional multiomics covariates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: learn interpretable communication-aware niche embeddings and spatial gene program activities
rows.Main Output: cell embeddings, niche labels, spatial gene program scores, atlas/reference mapping outputs
rows.Key Difference: Builds graph deep-learning niches around ligand-receptor, regulatory, and de novo spatial programs rather than composition-only clustering.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Genetics method paper and public code source. Layer 2 synthesis: retained here for niche/program embeddings; ligand-receptor edge inference or causal CCC interpretation routes to Cell-Cell Communication.
rows.Best First Choice When: When interpretable communication-aware niche or program embeddings are the endpoint and curated priors are acceptable.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is ligand-receptor edges, sender-receiver pairs, communication scores, or causal/pathway CCC interpretation.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: spatial graph with communication and regulatory programs
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Communication/regulatory priors can make embedding interpretation look mechanistic; treat LR or pathway claims as CCC-bound downstream interpretations, not Graph outputs.

rows.Main Input: single-cell and spatial transcriptomics profiles tokenized for a pretrained transformer model
rows.Main Use in This Topic: transfer or predict spatial context, niche labels, and neighborhood composition using foundation-model representations
rows.Main Output: foundation-model embeddings, spatial label predictions, neighborhood composition or density predictions
rows.Key Difference: Uses broad pretrained transformer representations instead of task-specific graph, covariance, or factorization models.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods paper and the article reports the model package and large pretraining resources. Layer 2 synthesis: high compute and model-prior caveats are critical for selection.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the analysis explicitly needs pretrained spatial/single-cell foundation-model transfer or spatial context prediction.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When a small interpretable niche table, hard domain label, or CCC edge list is the primary endpoint.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: pretrained cell representation with spatial-context tasks
rows.Interpretation Anchor: learned spatial context in transformer embeddings
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Foundation-model outputs can carry training-corpus bias and may be difficult to audit mechanistically.

rows.Main Input: spatial omics data for microenvironment-zone-specific cell-state analysis
rows.Main Use in This Topic: jointly represent cell states and cellular organization to identify microenvironment-zone-specific states
rows.Main Output: joint embeddings, soft clusters, microenvironment-zone-specific cell-state summaries
rows.Key Difference: Emphasizes joint embedding of cell states and cellular organization rather than standalone niche clustering or ecological metrics.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Cell Systems method paper; primary code trace is the upstream GitHub repository, with https://github.com/aifimmunology/SPARROW noted as an accessible fork/mirror. Layer 2 synthesis: retained for microenvironment-zone-specific cell states.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task asks how cell states vary across microenvironment zones or cellular organization contexts.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard domain labels, CCC edge inference, or topology motif discovery.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Zone-specific state claims depend on model assumptions, cell-state resolution, and tissue organization definitions; code access does not imply runtime support.

rows.Main Input: single-cell spatial maps with cell phenotypes, spatial coordinates, and optional sample labels
rows.Main Use in This Topic: discover unsupervised or supervised tissue cellular neighborhoods from cell phenotypes
rows.Main Output: tissue cellular neighborhood assignments and condition-specific TCN summaries
rows.Key Difference: Targets cell-phenotype neighborhood maps and can use sample labels for supervised condition-specific TCN discovery.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods method paper and code source. Layer 2 synthesis: retained here for tissue cellular neighborhoods; neighbor-preference scores or CCC-style interpretation route to Cell-Cell Communication.
rows.Best First Choice When: When segmented cell-phenotype maps are available and the endpoint is tissue cellular neighborhood discovery.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the main target is neighbor-preference scoring, ligand-receptor communication, pathway CCC, or hard tissue-domain labels.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Cell-phenotype labels can compress continuous states; supervised TCN associations and neighbor-preference interpretations need separate validation.

rows.Main Input: cell-type-labeled spatial neighborhood graph or spatial cell map
rows.Main Use in This Topic: discover overrepresented ordered spatial motifs in cellular architecture
rows.Main Output: spatial motif sequences/logos, motif locations, motif-associated expression summaries
rows.Key Difference: Searches graph paths for ordered spatial motifs instead of clustering neighborhoods into niches or factors.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology method paper; public code is traceable at the primary GitHub repository and archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14510210. Layer 2 synthesis: retained for motif/topology selection, with CCC/pathway interpretation treated as downstream only.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the endpoint is ordered spatial motif discovery in cellular architecture.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard tissue-domain labels, ligand-receptor CCC, pathway activity, or reconstructed spatial neighborhoods.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: ordered paths in a cell-type spatial graph
rows.Interpretation Anchor: ordered cell-type motifs and contextual expression
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Motif calls depend on graph construction and null models; pathway or CCC interpretation of motifs is downstream and not direct evidence.

rows.Method Family: Triangulation cellular community motif neural network
rows.Main Input: spatial omics or multiplexed cell maps with cell annotations, features, and spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify cellular community motifs and multicellular topological organization patterns
rows.Main Output: cellular community motifs, motif abundance summaries, phenotype-associated topological organization patterns
rows.Key Difference: Targets cellular community motifs in triangulated spatial graphs rather than ordered motif paths, TCN labels, niche clusters, or ecological diversity summaries.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper and public code/Zenodo trace, including archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15884334. Layer 2 synthesis: retained in the motif/topology branch, not as CCC or domain evidence.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the question asks for cellular community motifs or multicellular topological organization in spatial maps.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard tissue-domain labels, ligand-receptor CCC edges, or pathway causality.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Cell-type annotations, triangulation choices, and motif-size or query choices influence results; phenotype association is not causality.

rows.Main Input: single-cell-resolution spatial omics data with cell features and coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify and characterize cell niches at single-cell resolution
rows.Main Output: cell niche labels, niche representations, and niche marker or context summaries
rows.Key Difference: Learns multi-view graph representations for single-cell-resolution niches rather than broader niche clustering, TCN discovery, atlas-scale embeddings, or communication-prior programs.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper and public code/Zenodo trace, including archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14195486. Layer 2 synthesis: retained for cell-niche representation, not hard spatial-domain labeling.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the endpoint is single-cell-resolution niche identification and characterization from spatial omics.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is tissue-region/domain labels, ligand-receptor communication scores, or pathway CCC.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: multi-view cell and microenvironment graph representation
rows.Interpretation Anchor: single-cell-resolution niche composition and local context
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Niche labels depend on feature construction, graph views, and cell-state resolution; downstream biological interpretation needs validation.

rows.Main Input: atlas-scale spatial omics cell maps with cell features and spatial-proximity subgraphs
rows.Main Use in This Topic: learn microenvironment-aware cellular embeddings at atlas scale
rows.Main Output: cellular microenvironment embeddings, niche-context summaries, and downstream microenvironment labels
rows.Key Difference: Uses cell-centric spatial-proximity subgraphs and contrastive learning for atlas-scale microenvironment representation rather than smaller-scale niche clustering or foundation-model transfer.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the 2026 Nature Communications method paper and public GitHub/Zenodo trace, including archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19143524. Layer 2 synthesis: retained for atlas-scale cellular microenvironment representation only.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task needs atlas-scale cellular microenvironment embeddings or cell-centric context representation.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the required endpoint is hard tissue-domain labels, sender-receiver CCC, or a simple motif table.
rows.Interpretation Anchor: learned microenvironment context in cell embeddings
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Contrastive embeddings can encode cohort or platform bias and require validation before mechanism claims.

rows.Main Input: large-scale heterogeneous spatial omics data with cellular features and spatial context
rows.Main Use in This Topic: learn disentangled cellular embeddings that separate cell-intrinsic and spatial-context signals
rows.Main Output: disentangled cellular embeddings, spatial-context embeddings, and downstream context summaries
rows.Key Difference: Disentangles intracellular identity and extracellular or spatial-context signals rather than directly discovering motifs, niches, domains, or LR communication edges.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper and public GitHub/docs/Zenodo trace, including archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15860235. Layer 2 synthesis: retained as a spatial-context representation branch, not domain or CCC evidence.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task needs disentangled cellular embeddings that separate cell-intrinsic and neighborhood-context signals.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the primary endpoint is hard domain clustering, ligand-receptor/sender-receiver CCC, or pathway causal interpretation.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Disentanglement assumptions require validation; downstream clusters or interaction summaries are not mechanism proof.

rows.Main Input: spatial transcriptomics reference data plus single-cell RNA-seq query data
rows.Main Use in This Topic: reconstruct single-cell spatial neighborhoods and support 3D tissue visualization
rows.Main Output: stable matching neighbor graph, reconstructed spatial neighborhoods, 3D visualization coordinates
rows.Key Difference: Maps transcriptome-to-space relationships to reconstruct neighborhoods rather than clustering observed spatial neighborhoods directly.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology method paper and the article reports an R package and analysis code. Layer 2 synthesis: use in this topic is strongest for reconstruction, not de novo niche clustering.
rows.Best First Choice When: When spatial neighborhoods must be reconstructed for single-cell data using a spatial transcriptomics reference.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When no suitable spatial reference exists, or when the endpoint is hard domain labels, topology motifs, or CCC inference.
rows.Neighborhood Signal Unit: stable matching neighbor graph inferred from transcriptome-to-space projection
rows.Interpretation Anchor: spatial neighbor reconstruction and 3D tissue organization
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Reconstruction quality depends on reference match and may impose spatial structure absent from the query data.

rows.Main Input: spatial transcriptomics gene expression maps
rows.Main Use in This Topic: learn spatially informed gene representations from genomic context for downstream neighborhood-adjacent analyses
rows.Main Output: SIGEL-generated gene representations, spatial co-expression contexts, task-specific imputation/SVG/clustering outputs
rows.Key Difference: Produces gene-level spatial representations from expression-map context rather than cell- or niche-level labels first.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology paper and the article lists a public GitHub source location, while also containing a more conservative code-availability sentence. Layer 2 synthesis: code access is treated as available but flagged for audit.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task needs spatially informed gene embeddings or genomic-context features rather than cell-neighborhood labels.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the required output is hard domain labels, discrete cell niches, or CCC edges rather than gene-level context representations.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Gene embeddings are indirect neighborhood evidence and require downstream validation before biological mechanism claims.

rows.Method Family: Spatial niche colocalization and interaction-pattern analysis
rows.Main Input: spatial omics data with cell or spot features, spatial coordinates, and optional cell-type or phenotype annotations
rows.Main Use in This Topic: analyze spatial niches, colocalization patterns, and cellular interaction-pattern context
rows.Main Output: spatial niche labels or patterns, colocalization summaries, and interaction-context features
rows.Key Difference: Targets spatial niche and colocalization analysis directly, while keeping interaction-pattern language separate from ligand-receptor or causal communication claims.
rows.Evidence Source: DOI 10.1186/s13059-026-04069-z; Genome Biology method paper; code link supplied by targeted literature check
rows.Evidence Note: Direct DOI/publisher evidence verifies the SpaNiche method-paper identity and public code trace. Placement in Graph / Neighborhood is based on the niche, colocalization, and microenvironment endpoint; any interaction wording remains descriptive and branch-local.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the endpoint is spatial niche analysis with colocalization or microenvironment-pattern summaries.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the requested output is ligand-receptor edges, sender-receiver communication scores, pathway signaling, or causal CCC interpretation.
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Niche and colocalization patterns can reflect annotation, sampling density, graph construction, and spatial proximity; they should not be treated as causal or physical communication truth.

rows.Method Family: Multicellular motif discovery and molecular characterization
rows.Main Input: spatial omics data with cell or spot identities, molecular features, and spatial neighborhood structure
rows.Main Use in This Topic: discover and molecularly characterize multicellular motifs in spatial omics data
rows.Main Output: multicellular motif signatures and motif-associated molecular characterization
rows.Key Difference: Frames the problem as scalable motif query/discovery and molecular characterization rather than hard domain clustering or ligand-receptor communication.
rows.Evidence Source: bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.04.22.720136v1; code link supplied by targeted literature check
rows.Evidence Note: Preprint-only evidence verifies the SpatialQuery title and code trace. Inclusion is a targeted Graph / Neighborhood motif-branch correction; preprint status must remain visible before any positive formal display.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the endpoint is scalable discovery or querying of multicellular motifs and their molecular features.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the requested output is hard tissue-domain labels, ligand-receptor edges, or causal communication interpretation.
rows.Interpretation Anchor: multicellular motif structure and molecular characterization
rows.Scientific-risk Caveat: Preprint-only evidence; motif calls depend on graph construction, annotation quality, null models, and molecular follow-up, and do not establish causal interaction mechanisms.
